idiom_name: coordinator class with a Hash registry + stdlib Observable for the change fan-out
implementation_notes: Ruby expresses the pattern with a plain class: a Hash from view handle to view object, open() that registers a view built from a factories Hash and close() that deletes the entry before disposing of the view, plus the standard-library Observable mixin for the fan-out - changed followed by notify_observers(model) replaces the hand-written listener list, and observers may be objects with an update method or procs registered with :call. The container half comes from the toolkit: with ruby-gnome a Gtk::Notebook or Gtk::Stack performs the switching, and the coordinator keeps the handle-to-widget map that the toolkit does not track. The class form is still justified whenever view types are registered dynamically or view meta-operations must act on the whole set - the POSA shape with a Hash instead of a type registry; without that, a module with a Hash and a block-based fan-out is enough.
code_sketch:
require 'observer'
class ViewHandler
  include Observable                       # changed + notify_observers
  def initialize(factories) = @factories = factories
  def open(type, model)
    id = (@next_id = @next_id.to_i + 1).to_s
    (@open ||= {})[id] = @factories.fetch(type).call(model)   # create + register
    id                                     # handle, not the view
  end
  def close(id) = @open.delete(id).destroy  # unregister, then dispose
  def model_changed(model)
    changed; notify_observers(model)       # Observable needs changed first
  end
end
pitfalls: Observable keeps strong references to its observers and is not thread-safe: observers must be removed with delete_observer in close(), and a Mutex is needed when model changes can arrive from other threads.
notify_observers is silently a no-op unless changed was called first - a fan-out that 'does nothing' is almost always a missing changed.
Adding or deleting observers during notify_observers mutates the Hash the mixin iterates; register and unregister outside the notification pass.
Ruby's open classes make it easy for the coordinator to grow view-specific branches; keep per-view rendering in the view objects and the handler free of `case` statements over view types.
